Subject: Re: Increased latency + intermittent 502s from your JS SDK streaming (since 2.3.1)

Triage notes (initial):
- Reproduced locally using ripple_logs_0430 HAR. Root cause appears to be the JS SDK streaming parser when chunked transfers break across small websocket/http chunk boundaries.
- Specifically: when a header block is split such that CRLF is split across two TCP/chunk boundaries, our parser treats the partial header as a completed header and attempts to parse an invalid header line. That triggers a parse exception which bubbles to a 502 path in the runtime when not handled.
- The issue correlates with SDK v2.3.1 changes to the streaming parser which removed a small buffer-check optimization. v2.2.x does not exhibit this behavior.

Temporary mitigations we've validated for customers:
1) pin to SDK v2.2.x (fastest, low-risk).
2) server-side proxy that reassembles chunk boundaries (we can deploy a small reassembly filter temporarily).
3) increase client-side retry/backoff (band-aid).

Proposed fix:
- Reintroduce a buffer-and-wait behavior in the streaming parser: if a header line doesn't end with CRLF, buffer up to next chunk before parsing. Add robust defensive checks and unit tests for fragmented-CRLF cases.
- Unit + integration tests added for chunk boundary permutations.

I'll prepare a patch and a canary deployment plan in the next 90 minutes.

Folks — quick update and deployment plan. Patch and tests are ready (attached: sdk-parser-patch.diff). Summary:
- Root cause: streaming parser incorrectly parsing partial headers when chunk boundary splits CRLF.
- Fix: buffer partial lines until CRLF, add regression tests for split-CRLF and multiple-chunk headers.
- Canary plan: deploy patch to 2% of streaming traffic for 30 minutes in us-west, monitor error-rate and latency. If green, ramp to 25% then 100% over 90 minutes.
- Short-term mitigations: disabled the parser optimization that caused the regression; this increases CPU marginally but eliminates the 502 path.

We recommend Ripple Health: pin to SDK v2.2.x (immediate) OR allow us to enable a server-side reassembly proxy for the next 4 hours while we canary and roll the fix.

I'll schedule the canary at 11:00 PT unless we hear otherwise.

Marcus
